chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Burayd ibn Mu'awiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said:
Regarding the absent man, if he divorces his wife, she counts her waiting period (iddah) from the day he divorced her.
ai.seo_question: When does the waiting period begin for a wife if her husband is absent and divorces her?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies that the iddah for a wife of an absent husband begins immediately upon the husband's pronouncement of divorce, not upon her receipt of the news, a ruling derived from the consensus of the Imams. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the actual act of divorce as the triggering event for legal timelines, ensuring certainty in marital status during periods of separation.
